clue.text: Welsh singer in German comic opera and film

definitions.meaning: the pop star from Pontypridd famous for 'It's Not Unusual'
Edward German wrote a 1907 comic opera on Fielding's novel, and Tony Richardson's 1963 film of the same story won the Best Picture Oscar

explanation.surface: A singer from Wales appears in a German comic opera and a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' looks like a nationality but is the English composer Edward German; the novel's title names both his opera and the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Welsh entertainer and Fielding's foundling hero share this two-word name.

clue.text: Ball game tight, last of series

parts.note: a ball is round, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters of game reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A ball game finishing tight, the last match of a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' reads as describing a close contest, but it means drunk and so signals the anagram; 'Ball' gives the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the end of any series.

clue.text: Toy figure of missing sailor

parts.note: jumping a step means skipping or missing it
Jack (Jack Tar) is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A toy figure modelled on a sailor who has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A jointed puppet whose limbs fly up when its string is pulled is called by this name.

clue.text: A resident domestic

definitions.meaning: a citizen or subject of a country
relating to the home country rather than abroad, as in home news

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a citizen; as an adjective it means belonging to the country as a whole, not foreign.

clue.text: What Chippendale did with article for one very short of money?

indicators.note: the article is put in the place of one, the Roman numeral I, so one letter is swapped

parts.note: the Chippendales are a troupe of male strippers who take their clothes off for payment
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A joke question: what did Thomas Chippendale do with a piece of furniture, and was he broke?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chippendale' suggests the cabinetmaker, but it is a member of the stripping troupe; 'with article for one' swaps the I in STRIPPED for A.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being badly in need of money, as if bound tight by lack of funds.

clue.text: Language used by artist receiving stick

indicators.note: the artist's letters take in the stick, which sits inside them

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a wand is a thin stick, as a magician's

explanation.surface: A language used by a painter who has been given a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Also called Kinyarwanda, it is the Bantu tongue spoken in the central African country of the same name.

clue.text: Salad vegetable in a meal linked to recipe

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take
a dish is a course or meal served at table

explanation.surface: A salad vegetable appears in a meal tied to a particular recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent red-skinned root, sliced raw into salads.

clue.text: Short song from musical, hard going

indicators.note: going means departing, so the hard letter leaves the show's title

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A brief number from a stage musical proves hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard going' reads as a phrase meaning difficult, but 'hard' is H and 'going' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune or melody, especially a simple song, as in Bach's Air on the G String.

clue.text: Duke is vulgar, reportedly, in speech

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for vulgar is to be taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: coarse means crude or vulgar

explanation.surface: A duke is said to be crude in his talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal spoken or written communication on a subject, a lecture or address.

clue.text: A solitary Channel Island has it

parts.note: Herm is a small island in the Channel Islands, near Guernsey
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lone Channel Island possesses it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A solitary' looks like an adjective phrase about the island, but it is a noun: a person who lives alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse living alone, often for religious reasons; solitary is used here as a noun.

clue.text: Medical outfit embarrassed by trial

parts.note: embarrassment makes you go red in the face
a cross is a burden or trial to bear

explanation.surface: A medical team is put out by a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The international humanitarian organisation known for emergency medical aid.

clue.text: Prepare to take off one on duty

indicators.note: in this across clue one is put on the end of, after, the duty

parts.note: a duty is a tax levied on goods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A worker on duty gets ready for departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft move slowly along the ground to the runway before take-off.

clue.text: Rivalry in work station

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
a station is a post or position

explanation.surface: Competition breaks out in a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing or competing against someone is a state of contest.

clue.text: One qualified to handle a damaged plane?

definitions.text: One qualified to handle a damaged plane?

parts.words: One qualified to handle a damaged plane?
parts.note: the plane is not an aircraft but the tree, and the qualified person repairs trees as a doctor operates on patients

explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft engineer; it is the plane tree, tended by an arborist.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist who prunes and repairs damaged or diseased trees.

clue.text: Agents at resort do nothing

indicators.note: read as re-sort, the letters are sorted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Secret agents at a holiday resort are idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot but is re-sort, the anagram signal for AGENTS AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stay inactive and fail to develop.

clue.text: Colour ours quite garishly

indicators.note: garishly suggests something gaudy and jumbled, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone paints their property in a loud shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenish-blue shade named after the gemstone.

clue.text: High priest of unknown age outside

indicators.note: the age goes around the unknown letter

parts.note: an era is an age or period
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: A senior cleric of indeterminate age stands outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament priest and scribe who led the Jews back from Babylon.

clue.text: Don't need bubbly throughout

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizz, so the letters effervesce into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone declines champagne throughout the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like the champagne being refused but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: From one end right through to the other, along the whole length.

clue.text: Opera song from Callas needing no introduction

indicators.note: with no introduction the singer's first name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Maria Callas was the celebrated opera soprano

explanation.surface: An operatic number by Callas, a singer who needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' reads as praise for a famous diva but drops the first letter of MARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo song in an opera, the kind of showpiece Callas sang.

clue.text: Female, after I cast off, dressed

annotationWithheld.why: Female, after I cast off, dressed (8): the answer is F + IN + I + SHED, but no word is left for IN beside the definition; 'dressed' or 'cast off' would have to do two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Female, after I cast off, dressed

clue.text: Type of ring, we hear, for a young aquatic bird

indicators.note: we hear says the ring word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a signet ring bears a seal or initials

explanation.surface: A kind of ring, it seems, for a baby water bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the name for a baby swan, a young water bird in its first grey plumage.

clue.text: Country's revolutionary dance

parts.note: Turkey is the country
Trot is short for Trotskyist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: A nation's revolutionary folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragtime-era ballroom dance popular in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Runs excellent competition

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: Someone runs an excellent contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest of speed between competitors.

clue.text: Caught, she's out in game

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of she's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer is caught and she is out during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' reads as dismissal in cricket but is the anagram signal: SHES becomes HESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game of kings, queens and checkmate.

clue.text: Where Richmond is unspoilt, one small area

parts.note: virgin means untouched or unspoilt
I is the Roman numeral for one
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Richmond is a pristine spot, one little area.
explanation.walkthrough: Richmond suggests the London suburb, but it is the state capital of a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmond is the capital city of this US state.

clue.text: Fetch earl in car

indicators.note: in places the earl within the car

parts.note: GT is a gran turismo car

explanation.surface: Collect the nobleman sitting in his car.
explanation.definitionFit: To go and bring something back.

clue.text: Level, holding the Parisian football team

indicators.note: the level word holds the French article inside it

parts.note: even means level or flat
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A level team holding off the Paris football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side numbers this many players.

clue.text: Get going and defeat Italian

parts.note: to beat is to defeat

explanation.surface: Someone is told to clear off and beat the Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang command to go away or leave quickly.

clue.text: Playboy, fellow caught in armed hold-up

indicators.note: caught in means the fellow is trapped inside the robbery

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A playboy, a man trapped in an armed robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure-seeker devoted to indulgence, the stereotype of a playboy.
